findings.cause: The write rules match on the address text, and the second mount was never added to them.

findings.cause: The rules list who may change each listed area and allow everything not listed.
findings.dependencies: Every write route.
findings.verification: Probe section 1: 290 not refused before, 0 after (542 calls). Unit test "read-only roles change nothing, and may still ask questions that change nothing".
findings.evidence: qa/sim/baseline-probe.mjs section 1, run on commit 2d801ff: of 542 write calls made as AUDITOR and DATA_ANALYST, 290 were not refused; 28 succeeded outright, including creating jobs, order-hub orders and contacts, starting pipeline runs and changing demand settings.
findings.expected: A read-only role changes nothing. The code names these roles "readOnly".
findings.actual: Read-only roles were refused only where a department rule existed. Every route with no rule let them in.
findings.impact: An auditor or analyst login could change production, pricing set-up and master data.
findings.correction: Read-only roles are now refused on every changing request except a short list of requests that only ask a question (sign-in, the assistant, price calculations, form checks).
findings.requiredTests: Unit test and probe section 1, which covers every write route in the discovery file.

findings.cause: The access model was built on role and department only.
findings.dependencies: Every list and detail route; reports; the screens' branch pickers.
findings.where: Every route file under src/backend/src/routes; User.homeLocationId, UserLocation, UserDivision in schema.prisma
findings.evidence: Code: no route reads req.user.homeLocationId, UserLocation or UserDivision to limit a query (only routes/users.js scopes by organization, and only for user records). Database: UserLocation and UserDivision hold 0 rows after a full run. qa/sim/baseline-probe.mjs section 4: a login whose home branch has no stock read another branch's stock (200), listed and opened orders of every branch (200).
findings.expected: To be decided. The program brief describes tenant, division and location access as an existing architecture.
findings.actual: Branch, division and region are fields on records and filters on screens. They are not an access boundary: every staff login reads every branch, and changes any branch within its department.
findings.impact: At 80 branches every employee can see, and within their department change, every other branch's orders, stock, prices and customers.
findings.correction: Needs the owner's rule first: which roles are held to their own branch or region for reading, and which for changing. Then one scoping helper used by every route, and a sweep section that proves it.
findings.requiredTests: A sweep section: a branch login cannot read or change another branch's rows on every route that carries a location.

findings.cause: Rules were added for the core order-to-cash records only.
findings.dependencies: Scheduling, routing, quality records, documents.
findings.evidence: A saw-operator login was sent every write route (scratch probe, this session). Refused everywhere under orders, quotes, customers, invoices, shipments, products, grades, users, tax rates and the counter. findings.workflow: Work centers, assets, maintenance orders, partner admin, pricing override, executive, material tracking
findings.cause: No validation in the handler, and one catch-all reply.
findings.dependencies: Error monitoring; the screens' messages.
findings.verification: Probe section 3: 19 server errors before, 3 after (the 3 are B-006). Unit test "a change aimed at a missing record…".
findings.where: src/backend/src/middleware/safeErrors.js; src/backend/src/lib/db.js; routes/workCenters.js, assets.js, maintenanceOrders.js, salesRoutes.js, executive.js, materialTrackingRoutes.js, partner/adminRoutes.js
findings.evidence: qa/sim/baseline-probe.mjs section 3 on commit 2d801ff: 19 of 275 write routes answered an empty body or an unknown id with a 500.
findings.expected: An unknown record is a 404. Missing or wrong values are a 400. A 500 means the server is at fault.
findings.actual: These handlers catch every failure and answer 500, including "that record does not exist".
findings.impact: Staff see "failed" with no reason; monitoring cannot tell a typing mistake from an outage.
findings.correction: The reply layer now turns a failed change into 404 when the record was not there and 400 when the database layer refused the values, and logs the detail. One handler (new scenario) checks its name. Field-by-field validation in these handlers is still owed (see B-007).
findings.requiredTests: Unit test for the rule; probe section 3 with a ceiling that can only go down.

findings.cause: Prototype stores that were moved from memory into tables without being redesigned.
findings.dependencies: D-024, S-021, I-011 and the open decision card "Choose which stock list is the real one".
findings.module: Second stock list, order hub, stop work
findings.where: routes/inventoryV1.js + inventoryV1Store.js; routes/orderHubRoutes.js + orderHubStore.js; routes/stopWork.js + stopWorkStore.js
findings.evidence: Code read. Each keeps whole records as one JSON value per row. inventoryV1.js reloads five whole tables at the start of every request (refresh(), 13 call sites), changes the copies in memory and writes rows back one at a time with no transaction. /api/v1/inventory has its own adjust and transfer routes on stock that orders and shipping never see. The order hub has its own contacts, RFQs, quotes, orders and jobs.

findings.impact: Stock adjusted or transferred in the second list changes nothing the business ships from. At volume, each request to it reads every row.
findings.correction: The owner chooses the real one of each pair. Then the other is removed or made a view of the first.
findings.requiredTests: A two-requests-at-once test on whichever store is kept; the audit shows one stock list.

findings.cause: Sequential awaits.
findings.dependencies: Time tracking, labor costing, user administration.
findings.module: Users, shop-floor operations, job planning, material tracking, cockpit, partner carrier
findings.where: users.js (create, edit, delete, reset password), jobs.js (POST /:id/plan), operationsRoutes.js (start, complete, reassign), materialTrackingRoutes.js (staging ship), opsCockpit.js (accept recommendation), bomV1.js (PUT recipe), dispatchRoutes.js (delete work-center type), demandShaping.js, assets.js (seed), partner/carrierRoutes.js (proof of delivery)
findings.evidence: Discovery count: 16 handlers make two or more database changes outside a transaction (qa/enterprise-excellence/api-inventory.md lists them). Read in full: operationsRoutes.js start (three changes in sequence) and complete.
findings.expected: Changes that belong together are saved together or not at all.
findings.actual: A failure between two changes leaves the first one saved. Example: an operation is marked started and its time log is not created.
findings.impact: Time logs, user role assignments and job plans can be half-saved after an error.
findings.correction: Wrap each in one transaction.
findings.requiredTests: A test per handler that fails the second change and checks the first was not kept.

findings.cause: No move table for operations.
findings.dependencies: Time tracking, schedule, job status.
findings.evidence: Code read: neither checks the operation's present status. A completed operation can be started again; an operation can be completed twice or without having started.
findings.expected: An operation follows not-started, running, paused, complete (lib/workflowRules.js does this for jobs, orders and shipments).
findings.actual: Any call is accepted.
findings.impact: Actual start and end times and the time logs can be overwritten; labor time is unreliable.
findings.correction: A move table for operations in lib/workflowRules.js. Whether a completed operation may be reopened for rework is the owner's rule (extends M-017).
findings.requiredTests: Unit tests for the table; a sweep check per refused move.

findings.cause: Lists written for a demo-sized database.
findings.dependencies: Screens that expect the whole list.

Read and confirmed: GET /api/products returns the whole catalogue; GET /api/staff/operators returns every operator with skills; GET /api/work-centers every work center. The rest are candidates from the code scan and have not each been read.

findings.actual: Some are small set-up lists where no limit is harmless; others grow with products, operators and partners.
findings.impact: Response size and time grow with the data at 80 branches.
findings.correction: Read each of the 58; give the growing ones a limit and paging, and record the fixed-size ones as accepted.
findings.requiredTests: The existing "bounded lists" sweep check extended to these routes.

findings.cause: Tests were built around the order-to-cash path first.
findings.dependencies: Every later phase relies on these gates.

The other 247 write routes have only ever been called by tests that expect a refusal. There are no frontend unit tests. The GitHub check runs the unit tests, the screen audit and lint; the simulation, sweep and browser suites need a database and run only on a developer machine.

findings.cause: Schema written ahead of the features.
findings.dependencies: X-009 decides which modules are built.
findings.evidence: Discovery: 52 of 157 tables are read or written by no server code (41 safety tables, 11 maintenance, approvals, commodity prices and others). After a full simulation run 96 of 158 tables in the QA database are empty. 160 columns hold free-form JSON, which the database cannot check.
findings.expected: A table exists because something uses it.
findings.actual: A third of the schema is design that was never built (see X-009).
findings.impact: Migrations, backups and reviews carry tables that mean nothing; the schema overstates what the product does.
findings.correction: After the X-009 decisions, drop the tables of modules that will not be built. Dropping tables is a destructive change and needs the owner's approval and a SQL Editor file.
findings.requiredTests: The inventory shows no table without code.

findings.cause: The hosted server runs per request; nothing runs between requests.
findings.dependencies: Any future integration that needs scheduled work (email, statements, replenishment, overdue invoices).
findings.statusNote: Needs a scheduled trigger on the host, which is the owner's setting
findings.evidence: Code read: a failed delivery is marked RETRYING with a next-retry time, and processPendingRetries() would resend it. Nothing calls that function (no import, no schedule), and the server has no scheduler, queue or background worker of any kind.
findings.expected: A failed delivery is retried.
findings.actual: It is marked for retry and never sent again.
findings.impact: A partner that was briefly unreachable never receives the event.
findings.correction: A scheduled trigger on the host that calls the retry function. Setting up a schedule on the host is the owner's.
findings.requiredTests: A test that fails a delivery, runs the retry and sees it delivered.

findings.cause: Per-request hosting and no provider chosen.
findings.evidence: Discovery: no scheduler, queue, worker, event bus or email or text provider exists in the server code. Nothing is sent to a customer or a colleague by the system (D-033, D-034); exception records are created only when a person or a request creates them; an expired quote or an overdue invoice is worked out when someone looks at it and nobody is told.
findings.expected: To be decided per function.
findings.actual: Everything happens only when someone opens a screen or presses a button.
findings.impact: No reminders, no escalation, no automatic status by date, no customer notification.
findings.correction: Choose the provider and the host schedule; then build each timed function.
findings.requiredTests: Per function.

findings.dependencies: None.
findings.where: npm run lint at the repository root
findings.evidence: Root lint, this session: 1,524 warnings. 1,438 unused variables or imports, 39 React effects whose dependency list does not match what they use (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps), 20 needless escapes, 17 declarations inside case blocks, 4 empty blocks, 3 needless catches, 2 list items with no key.

findings.cause: The quick sale was built as a priced receipt on top of orders and invoices; stock for items priced each was left out and the void marker was put in the notes.
findings.dependencies: The owner: are shelf items counted stock? I-016 (no stock adjustment).
findings.evidence: Code read and the QA database after three simulation cycles: a finished counter quick sale is a COMPLETE order whose lines say they shipped, with no shipment, no stock movement and no change to any stock level. A voided sale is still COMPLETE; the void is the word VOIDED added to the order notes, plus a credit memo and a refund. qa/tools/db-facts.mjs counts these lines separately.
findings.expected: A rule, written down: either shelf items are counted stock and a sale reduces it (and a void puts it back), or they are not counted and the system says so. A void that reports can filter on without reading free text.
findings.actual: Shelf items sold at the counter never reduce stock. Any report that filters on order status counts a voided sale as a completed one; only the counter's own daily figures read the note.
findings.impact: Shelf stock cannot be trusted if it is ever counted in the system. Sales reports by order status overstate by the voided sales (the money side is correct: the credit memo and refund exist).
findings.correction: After the decision: record a stock movement on sale and on void, and give a voided sale its own status or flag.
findings.requiredTests: Simulation: a counter sale reduces the shelf item and a void restores it; reports exclude voided sales.

findings.evidence: Sim: "create sales order", "order created by the signed-in user". Baseline `baseline-1001.json`.
findings.actual: Creating a sales order through `POST /api/orders` failed with a server error unless the browser sent the id of the user creating it. Whatever id was sent was trusted. 46 of 50 baseline jobs stopped here.
findings.cause: The route wrote the request body straight into the database.
findings.correction: The signed-in user is the creator. Only listed fields are accepted. Lines, prices and totals are validated. `routes/orders.js`
findings.verification: Sim: "create sales order", "order created by the signed-in user". Baseline `baseline-1001.json`.

findings.evidence: Sim: books checks after every shipment; whole-database reconciliation.
findings.actual: Dispatching a shipment changed nothing else. The order line's shipped quantity, the line and order status, and stock all stayed as they were, so orders never completed and stock never went down.
findings.cause: Dispatch only set the shipment's own status.
findings.correction: Dispatch now updates the lines, sets the order to PARTIAL or COMPLETE, takes the reserved stock out and writes a stock movement, in one transaction. `routes/shipments.js`
findings.verification: Sim: books checks after every shipment; whole-database reconciliation.

findings.evidence: Sim: over-reservation refused; race probe "exactly one wins"; reconciliation (no negatives).
findings.actual: Stock could be reserved without limit: more than was available, more than the order line needed, on cancelled orders, with zero or negative quantities. Available stock could go negative.
findings.cause: No checks on `POST /api/orders/:id/allocate`.
findings.correction: All of those are refused. The update only succeeds while enough is available, so two requests cannot both take the last of it.
findings.verification: Sim: over-reservation refused; race probe "exactly one wins"; reconciliation (no negatives).

findings.evidence: Unit: 6 order tests. Sim: reopen refused, cancel releases stock.
findings.actual: Any order status could be written by hand, including reopening a cancelled order or marking an order complete. Cancelling left its stock reserved for ever.
findings.cause: No status rules.
findings.correction: Status table in `lib/workflowRules.js`. Cancelling releases reservations and cancels the lines.
findings.verification: Unit: 6 order tests. Sim: reopen refused, cancel releases stock.

findings.evidence: Unit: shipment tests. Sim: double-ship, over-ship, deliver-before-dispatch refused; triple-dispatch probe.
findings.actual: A shipment could be delivered without ever leaving, dispatched more than once, created for a draft or cancelled order, or carry more than was ordered. Shipment lines were not saved at all.
findings.cause: `POST /api/shipments` wrote the raw body; dispatch and deliver had no checks.
findings.correction: Shipments need a CONFIRMED or PARTIAL order, valid lines and quantities within what is left. Dispatch and deliver follow a status table and are safe against double-clicks. Added the item and status routes the logistics screens already call.
findings.verification: Unit: shipment tests. Sim: double-ship, over-ship, deliver-before-dispatch refused; triple-dispatch probe.

findings.evidence: Unit: 7 numbering tests. Probes: 10 simultaneous orders and 10 simultaneous jobs, all distinct.
findings.actual: Order, job, shipment and web-order numbers were "row count + 1". Two people saving at the same moment got the same number and one save failed.
findings.cause: Counting rows is not a sequence.
findings.correction: `lib/numbering.js` retries with the next number when the database reports a duplicate. Applied to sales orders (the order API, order intake, accepted web orders and POS), jobs (both places they are created), shipments and web orders.
findings.verification: Unit: 7 numbering tests. Probes: 10 simultaneous orders and 10 simultaneous jobs, all distinct.

findings.actual: Work orders, QC inspections, maintenance orders and operator codes were also numbered "row count + 1".
findings.cause: Same as D-006.
findings.correction: Those four now use `lib/numbering.js`. Quotes and RFQs are left with D-019, because those routes are broken anyway. (Follow-up PR)
findings.verification: Unit: numbering tests.

findings.evidence: Sim: transfers-receiving category (15 jobs in the final cycles). Reconciliation: "one location per item".
findings.actual: Receiving and transferring stock failed with a server error unless the browser sent a user id. Negative receipts were accepted. A transfer ignored where the item actually was and moved only one of the two records that hold its location.
findings.cause: Raw body written to the database; two tables hold the location.
findings.correction: Signed-in user recorded. Quantity must be above zero. From-location must match. Both records move together. `routes/inventory.js`
findings.verification: Sim: transfers-receiving category (15 jobs in the final cycles). Reconciliation: "one location per item".

findings.evidence: Unit: 5 job tests plus "every move the job board offers is accepted by the server". Sim: exception category.
